decisions.reason: It is highly related to the firm's core authentication and trusted second-channel know-how, and the lack of recent standalone visibility is more consistent with bundling into broader solutions than with abandoning the capability.

Mobile PDF signing fits the firm's direction toward online contract signing and can be improved with existing identity and authorization knowledge, so the firm is still likely to retain it despite weaker standalone visibility.

A multi-layer end-to-end security architecture is central to the firm's cryptography and platform base, so absorptive capacity strongly favors keeping it even if it is no longer marketed prominently as a separate product.

This is a narrower use-case product, and two years without website evidence suggest the firm will likely reallocate resources from this niche standalone offer into broader secure-communication products.
Although related to the firm's security expertise, the hardware-based token is less central to its software-led identity strategy, and prolonged low visibility points to likely withdrawal.

Payment security compliance remains close to the firm's regulated transaction-security competences, so it is still worth retaining, though probably increasingly embedded within a broader platform or service package.
